+"""Request handlers."""
+
+import re
+
+from app.services import users
+
+_DOMAIN_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9.-]+")
+
+
+def handle_get_user(params: dict) -> tuple[int, dict]:
+    raw = params.get("id")
+    if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw.isdigit():
+        return 400, {"error": "invalid id"}
+    user = users.get_user(int(raw))

+    return 200, user

+    domain = params.get("domain")
+    if not isinstance(domain, str) or _DOMAIN_RE.fullmatch(domain) is None:
+        return 400, {"error": "invalid domain"}
+    return 200, {"users": users.get_users_by_domain(domain)}

+"""SQLite persistence for users."""
+
+import sqlite3
+
+_conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:", check_same_thread=False)
+_conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
+_conn.execute("CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE)")
+_conn.executemany("INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", [
+    (1, "Ada Lovelace", "ada@example.com"),
+    (2, "Linus Torvalds", "linus@example.com"),
+    (3, "Grace Hopper", "grace@example.com"),
+])
+_conn.commit()
+
+
+def _to_dict(row):
+    return dict(row) if row else None
+
+
+def get_by_id(user_id: int) -> dict | None:
+    return _to_dict(_conn.execute("SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)).fetchone())
+
+
+def find_by_email(email: str) -> dict | None:
+    return _to_dict(_conn.execute("SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE email = ?", (email,)).fetchone())
+
+
+def list_by_domain(domain: str) -> list[dict]:
+    """Return users whose email is at exactly the given domain, ordered by id."""
+    rows = _conn.execute(
+        "SELECT id, name, email FROM users "
+        "WHERE lower(substr(email, instr(email, '@') + 1)) = lower(?) "
+        "ORDER BY id",
+        (domain,),
+    ).fetchall()
+    return [dict(row) for row in rows]

=== scripts/digest.py ===
"""Print the size and SHA-256 of a file as JSON. Usage: python scripts/digest.py --file PATH"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--file", required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()
data = Path(args.file).read_bytes()
print(json.dumps({"file": args.file, "bytes": len(data), "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()}))
=== scripts/report.py ===
"""Print a small JSON report for a name. Usage: python scripts/report.py --name NAME"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--name", required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()
print(json.dumps({"name": args.name, "length": len(args.name),
                  "checksum": hashlib.sha256(args.name.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]}))

"""Print a URL slug for a title as JSON. Usage: python scripts/slug.py --title TITLE"""

import argparse
import json
import re

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--title", required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()
print(json.dumps({"slug": re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", args.title.lower()).strip("-")}))

from app.db import store
from app.api.handlers import handle_users_by_domain

# add tricky rows directly to the in-memory db for this process
store._conn.executemany(
    "INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
    [
        (4, "Sub", "sub@sub.example.com"),
        (5, "Case", "CASE@EXAMPLE.COM"),
        (6, "Suffix", "x@notexample.com"),
        (7, "Dash", "d@my-site.co.uk"),
    ],
)
store._conn.commit()

def emails(res):
    return [u["email"] for u in res[1]["users"]]

# 200 exact match, case-insensitive, ordered by id
r = handle_users_by_domain({"domain": "example.com"})
print("example.com", r[0], emails(r))
assert r[0] == 200
assert emails(r) == ["ada@example.com", "linus@example.com", "grace@example.com", "CASE@EXAMPLE.COM"], emails(r)
assert [u["id"] for u in r[1]["users"]] == [1, 2, 3, 5]

# case-insensitive input
r = handle_users_by_domain({"domain": "EXAMPLE.COM"})
assert r[0] == 200 and emails(r) == ["ada@example.com", "linus@example.com", "grace@example.com", "CASE@EXAMPLE.COM"]

# subdomain must not match parent
r = handle_users_by_domain({"domain": "sub.example.com"})
assert r[0] == 200 and emails(r) == ["sub@sub.example.com"], emails(r)

# suffix must not match
r = handle_users_by_domain({"domain": "ample.com"})
assert r[0] == 200 and emails(r) == [], emails(r)
r = handle_users_by_domain({"domain": "notexample.com"})
assert r[0] == 200 and emails(r) == ["x@notexample.com"], emails(r)

# hyphens/dots/digits allowed
r = handle_users_by_domain({"domain": "my-site.co.uk"})
assert r[0] == 200 and emails(r) == ["d@my-site.co.uk"], emails(r)

# invalid inputs
for bad in [None, 123, "", "exa mple.com", "exa_mple.com", "exämple.com", "example.com; DROP", "@", "a@b.com", "exa/mple.com", "exa+mple.com", "exa@mple.com", "exa\tmple.com"]:
    res = handle_users_by_domain({"domain": bad})
    assert res == (400, {"error": "invalid domain"}), (bad, res)

# missing key entirely
assert handle_users_by_domain({}) == (400, {"error": "invalid domain"})

# valid but no users
assert handle_users_by_domain({"domain": "none.com"}) == (200, {"users": []})

print("ALL OK")
